title: AI Engineering
tagline: The real stack behind production AI products: prompting, retrieval, agents, tool use, structured outputs, and evaluation, applied to a real shipped product, not a toy chatbot.

modules.title: Orientation
modules.summary: What this field actually is, what people in it actually build, where you might fit, and exactly what the next 8 modules will (and won’t) teach you.

modules.title: Prompting & Structured Outputs
modules.summary: A language model produces text. Your program needs data. This module closes that gap reliably, not with a nicer-sounding prompt, but with validation and repair logic that doesn’t trust the model to behave.

modules.title: Context Windows & Token Economics
modules.summary: Every prompt has a budget, measured in tokens, not characters or “how much text feels reasonable.” The actual arithmetic for what fits, what it costs, and what to do when your content doesn’t fit.

modules.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
modules.summary: A model only knows what’s in its prompt. Retrieval decides, out of everything you could put there, which pieces actually get in, by searching, not by hoping the right chunk made the cut.

modules.title: Tool Use & Function Calling
modules.summary: A model can only produce text. Everything it does beyond that, looking something up, sending an email, charging a card, happens because a tool call it generated got executed by your code. That execution step is where correctness and safety actually live.

modules.title: Agent Architectures & Control Flow
modules.summary: An agent is what happens when a model chains steps together, reasoning about each result before deciding the next action, in a loop it controls. That loop needs boundaries, or it doesn’t stop on its own.

modules.title: Reliability for LLM Systems
modules.summary: Model APIs fail: rate limits, timeouts, transient server errors. Some failures are worth retrying, some never will succeed no matter how many times you try, and treating them the same wastes time, money, and your users’ patience.

modules.title: Evaluation, Testing & Observability
modules.summary: “I tried a few prompts and it looked good” isn’t evaluation, it’s a vibe check on a handful of lucky examples. A systematic way to measure whether a system is actually working, and whether a change made it better or worse.

modules.title: Capstone: A Production AI Agent
modules.summary: A client brief: a support bot that must answer from a knowledge base, act on tools safely, run inside a bounded loop, and survive a flaky model API, graded against a rubric, not vibes.

whyItMatters: Retrieval can ground an LLM on information outside its training data.
Tool use lets an AI system interact with external systems, not just generate text.
Evaluation is necessary because a response that sounds right can still be wrong.
Prompting is only one part of a production AI system.
Cost and latency become real engineering constraints once an AI application scales.
